question: Which recipe generates TRULY multi-modal (detectable K!=1) expert trajectories?
setup: Four injection recipes under one dynamics frame, each with true K=3 (except D = noise control K=1): A multi-expert weights, B hidden intent, C committed role (temporal phase), D random noise. Windows are SequenceMixture-compatible.

separability_probe.interpretation: A/B/C ALL generate truly multi-modal trajectories: episode-level (whole-trajectory mean action+effect) classifies z perfectly (1.00). The SequenceMixture detector FAILS to recover K=3 (gives 1-2) because it does per-WINDOW posterior with a reconstruction loss that does not aggregate to the trajectory level - the z signature is only fully visible over the whole episode (esp. C, whose z is a segment-sequence offset; single windows inside a segment carry little z). D (noise) is correctly K=1 (no structure).
separability_probe.conclusion: For generating truly multi-modal expert data, A (multi-expert weights) and B (hidden intent) are the most feasible: simplest and window-classifiable-adjacent; C needs trajectory-level (not window-level) aggregation to be discoverable. The real bottleneck is the DISCOVERY side: per-window SequenceMixture cannot recover trajectory-level tactics - need trajectory-level discrete latent (CVAE/1903.10304 style) or window posterior + episode aggregation, exactly as the literature recommended.
